overview: Two anaerobic, spore-forming Gram-positive rods whose potent neurotoxins produce opposite clinical pictures — rigid spasm versus flaccid paralysis.
genZNote: Tetanus locks you up. Botulism shuts you down.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: An anaerobic, spore-forming Gram-positive rod that produces tetanospasmin, causing tetanus.
aspects.valueB: An anaerobic, spore-forming Gram-positive rod that produces botulinum toxin, causing botulism.

aspects.label: Toxin Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Tetanospasmin blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters (GABA, glycine) at spinal synapses, causing sustained muscle contraction (spastic paralysis).
aspects.valueB: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, causing flaccid paralysis.

aspects.label: Clinical Presentation
aspects.valueA: Muscle rigidity, lockjaw (trismus), risus sardonicus, and generalized muscle spasms.
aspects.valueB: Descending flaccid paralysis, diplopia, dysphagia, and respiratory failure in severe cases.

aspects.label: Route of Entry
aspects.valueA: Deep, contaminated puncture wounds where anaerobic conditions favor spore germination.
aspects.valueB: Ingestion of preformed toxin (improperly canned food), wound contamination, or intestinal colonization in infants (honey exposure).

aspects.label: Prevention
aspects.valueA: Tetanus toxoid vaccine (part of routine DTaP/Tdap immunization).
aspects.valueB: Avoiding improperly canned/preserved foods; no toxoid vaccine in routine use.

aspects.label: Treatment Considerations
aspects.valueA: Wound debridement, tetanus immune globulin, and toxoid booster.
aspects.valueB: Antitoxin administration and supportive respiratory care.
